//: 'Split-mu' braking — left wheels on dry asphalt, right wheels on ice.
//1: Standard automotive validation test for ABS yaw stability.  Without
//2: individual-wheel ABS control, the asphalt-side wheels grip while
//3: the ice-side wheels lock — net result is a yawing moment that pulls
//4: the car toward the high-mu side.  Per-wheel ABS modulation lets
//5: each side use its own friction limit.
//7: Watch the yaw_rate column in the CSV.  BTCM-on should keep yaw
//8: near zero (car stays straight); BTCM-off should drift positive
//11: THE LAUNCH MUST NOT WRITE THE ANSWER.  The runway used to be 60 m,
//12: and the pre-boundary half of this scenario needs 130 m of it
//13: (78.4 m to reach 20 m/s, then 51.6 m of settle).  So the car
//14: straddled the seam at 40 mph under full throttle: the ice-side spun
//15: against the asphalt-side wheels (peak |slip| 0.71) and the car had
//16: already yawed 3.4 degrees before the brake event started — on the
//17: one test whose verdict IS the yaw.  The runway now covers the whole
//18: pre-brake half (see level/flat_split_mu.json for the distance
//19: budget): entry speed and a 2.60 s / 51.6 m settle both land on
//20: uniform asphalt, the car crosses onto the split coasting at
//21: 19.47 m/s and 0.37 deg of yaw, and settles a further 2.72 s /
//22: 52.2 m ON the split before the brake.  Measured yaw carried into
//23: the brake event: 1.37 deg, down from 3.41 deg, with yaw RATE at
//24: 0.00002 deg/s — the car is straight and no longer turning.  What
//25: remains is the one-off heading step the split's own coast-drag
//26: asymmetry produces in the first ~1.2 s on the surface, which is
//27: this test's physics rather than its launch.
//29: The brake application is unchanged — same full 1.0, same 13 s hold.
//30: Every event from the brake onward is shifted +3 s to sit after the
//34: left half asphalt 0.9, right half ice 0.08).
name: abs_split_mu

events.//1: that spins the drive wheels from a dead stop; see the PR

events.//: Settle on asphalt, cross onto the split, settle again, then brake.
